facts.text: I was referred because my blood calcium is low.
I've had spasms in my face.
I've had attacks where my muscles go into spasm (tetany).
I've had leg cramps.

facts.item: when the spasms and cramps started
facts.text: The face spasms, muscle spasms and leg cramps started when I was about 10.

facts.item: course of the spasms and cramps
facts.text: They got better during puberty but came back when I was an adult, which is why I was first tested.
I take vitamin D by mouth.
I take calcium tablets.
Since starting the vitamin D and calcium, my symptoms have been relieved and I was told my calcium came back to normal.
Since I was 4 I've had moderate hearing loss in both ears (sensorineural), and I wear hearing aids.
I was born very small, weighing 1114 grams.
I was born with drooping eyelids.
I was born with joint contractures, joints that were stiff and bent.
I didn't have any lack of oxygen at birth.
I wasn't born with any brain abnormalities.
No one in my family has parathyroid disease.
No one in my family has had tetany.
No one in my family is deaf.
No one in my family has malformed kidneys (kidney dysplasia).
No one in my family has birth defects.
I'm Japanese.

findings.name: serum calcium and phosphate
findings.result: Calcium 8.3 mg/dL; phosphate 4.9 mg/dL (on vitamin D and calcium supplementation).

findings.name: serum calcium and phosphate at the initial evaluation
findings.result: Adjusted serum calcium 6.1 mg/dL (normal 8.8–10.1); phosphate 5.4 mg/dL (normal 2.7–4.6).
findings.time: initial evaluation in adulthood, before vitamin D and calcium were started

aliases: hypoparathyroidism, deafness and renal dysplasia syndrome
hypoparathyroidism, sensorineural deafness and renal disease syndrome
gold.reasoning: 1. Kenny–Caffey syndrome was considered as a congenital cause of hypoparathyroidism — “Differential diagnosis of early‐onset hypoparathyroidism includes several congenital diseases, DiGeorge syndrome, Kenny‐Caffey syndrome, and a genetic abnormality in PTH or CaSR...” 2. Genetic abnormalities in PTH or the calcium‐sensing receptor were considered in the differential — “Differential diagnosis of early‐onset hypoparathyroidism includes ... a genetic abnormality in PTH or CaSR...” 3. HDR syndrome was suspected because of the combination of hypoparathyroidism and sensorineural hearing loss, “... deafness is almost always observed in HDR syndrome and more rarely in DiGeorge syndrome.”
